A page for every ad, built to book.

A landing page is a single page built for one ad and one action. Bookdzilla builds pages that repeat the promise of the ad, show your reviews on the first screen and put booking one tap away, so more of the clicks you pay for become inquiries.

Signs your page is the leak.

  • The ad offers a free design visit and the page it opens never mentions it.
  • You have hundreds of five-star reviews on Google and none on the page.
  • The form sits three screens down on a phone.
  • There is no starting price, so people leave to find one somewhere else.
  • The page takes several seconds to load on mobile data.

What goes on every page.

  • The promise, repeated

    The headline says what the ad said, so the visitor knows they are in the right place.

  • Proof on the first screen

    Your Google rating, the review count and one short review beside the button.

  • A realistic price

    A starting price or a range you are comfortable sharing. It filters and reassures.

  • One action

    A short form or two open times, visible without scrolling on a phone.

  • A second offer

    A price guide or an open-dates check for people who are not ready to book today.

Questions about landing pages.

  • What is the difference between a landing page and a homepage?

    A homepage serves every visitor and links everywhere. A landing page serves one ad and asks for one action. Because it repeats the promise of the ad and removes other choices, more visitors take that action.

  • Do we have to rebuild our website?

    No. Your site stays. We add landing pages next to it and connect them to your form, phone and calendar.

  • We do not publish prices. Is that a problem?

    No. A starting price or a range such as "most projects land between" is enough. Full pricing can wait for the visit or the call.

  • How many pages do we need?

    One for each distinct promise you advertise. Most businesses start with two or three.
